text:
Vladislav Gavrikov is the steady, unflashy partner on the Rangers' blue line, logging about 21.5 minutes a night and blocking 41 shots. The Rangers get almost 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, nearly four points better than without him, so the defense is working.

The offense isn't, at least on the scoresheet. One goal and seven points in 22 games, and just one assist in his last ten, is a long way from last season, when he scored 14 goals and 35 points. That was a career year by the goals column, and Evolving-Hockey's numbers suggest it wasn't built on luck: they had him at 0.7 expected wins against -0.7 actual, meaning the chances were there but the finishing and goaltending around him weren't.

This season his own chances have shrunk (1.06 expected goals), and he is shooting 3.2%. Some of that comes back; our range has him around 30 points. The Rangers have had nearly a week off since beating Montreal on Nov. 16. For a sixth-round pick who has made it work in three cities, this role is the job.
